sections.heading: Permits, provisional licensing and transfers
sections.markdown:
## Permits, provisional licensing and transfers

FACT_ID: sec02-R01 | anchor: A01
A first Class C license requires the REAL ID documentation standards if the applicant has not already satisfied them. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=10]

FACT_ID: sec02-R02 | anchor: A01
At age 18, a Class D holder may seek Class C after holding a valid Class D until that age or for one year and one day, with no major-traffic-violation conviction during the preceding 12 months. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=10]

FACT_ID: sec02-R03 | anchor: A01
A qualified United States citizen exchanging Class D for Class C must surrender the earlier credential or affirm inability to do so; the handbook requires no additional documents or testing for that exchange. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=10]

FACT_ID: sec02-R04 | anchor: A01
A CP holder must be at least 18 to exchange the permit for Class C, surrender the permit or affirm inability to surrender it, and pass the road driving test. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=10]

FACT_ID: sec02-R05 | anchor: A01
The CP-to-Class-C applicant must sign an affidavit documenting 40 hours of supervised driving, including 6 nighttime hours. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=10]

FACT_ID: sec02-R06 | anchor: A01
An unlicensed applicant aged at least 18 may apply directly for Class C by meeting document requirements, passing the knowledge and road examinations, and attesting to 40 supervised driving hours including 6 at night. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=10]

FACT_ID: sec02-R07 | anchor: A01
An adult who wants supervised practice before full licensing may instead obtain a Class C instructional permit. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=10]

FACT_ID: sec02-R08 | anchor: A02
A new Georgia resident who wants to drive must apply for the Georgia license or permit within 30 days of establishing residency, subject to the handbook's stated exceptions. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=11]

FACT_ID: sec02-R09 | anchor: A03
A new resident without a valid out-of-state permit or license follows Georgia's first-issuance process, with the appropriate teen or adult requirements. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=12]

FACT_ID: sec02-R10 | anchor: A03
A transfer applicant younger than 18 with a valid license or permit from another state or the District of Columbia normally qualifies for a comparable Georgia document only after meeting Georgia school, driver-education and awareness-program conditions. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=12]

FACT_ID: sec02-R11 | anchor: A03
For the adult state-to-state transfer route, the earlier license must be surrendered and must not have been expired for 2 years or more. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=12]

FACT_ID: sec02-R12 | anchor: A03
If an adult transfer applicant cannot surrender the earlier valid license, the handbook requires a certified driving history from the issuing state, dated within 30 days and showing valid status. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=12]

FACT_ID: sec02-R13 | anchor: A03
The regular transfer minimum is age 18. A 17-year-old may transfer an equivalent valid Class C license only when it has no restrictions on time, route, driving purpose or passengers. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=12]

FACT_ID: sec02-R14 | anchor: A03
An adult transfer applicant must provide the full Social Security number for verification, identity and citizenship or lawful-presence evidence, 2 Georgia residence documents, and pass a vision screening. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=12]

FACT_ID: sec02-R15 | anchor: A03
Transfer identity and lawful-presence documents must be originals or certified copies; a fax is not acceptable. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=12]

FACT_ID: sec02-R16 | anchor: A03
For a foreign credential missing from the applicant's possession, the handbook calls for an English-language driving history from the issuing country dated within the last 30 days. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=12]

FACT_ID: sec02-R17 | anchor: A03
Most noncitizens may keep a valid foreign driving or identification document after Georgia issues its equivalent. A United States citizen must surrender foreign-issued driving and identification credentials. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=12]

FACT_ID: sec02-R18 | anchor: A03
A document issued outside the United States states and the District of Columbia is generally processed as a new Georgia issuance, including the examinations applicable to the requested class and required identity, lawful-presence, Social Security and residence evidence. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=12]

FACT_ID: sec02-R19 | anchor: A03
Foreign-country applicants ordinarily complete knowledge, road and vision examinations; some countries have testing exemptions listed by DDS. The handbook does not identify those countries on this page. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=12]

FACT_ID: sec02-R20 | anchor: A03
Applicants younger than 18 transferring from outside the country must also satisfy the additional teen-licensing requirements. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=12]

FACT_ID: sec02-R21 | anchor: A03
The handbook warns that privately operated sites may charge for information or training. It identifies the DDS government website as the official Georgia licensing source. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=12]

Misconceptions: The provisional passenger limits change over successive periods; the adult transfer exception is not a blanket waiver for every teen.
Mnemonic: Credential, age, holding period, documents, tests.
Glossary: An affidavit is the signed certification required for the stated driving experience; a comparable transfer remains subject to Georgia conditions.
Dynamic-fact isolation: Permit duration, fees, foreign-country reciprocity and current document policies require current issuer confirmation.

ranked.label: Apply the correct permit supervision rule

verification_debt.claim_text: The dated handbook facts retain source freshness, rights and independent factual-review debt; no current-law equivalence or live service/fee policy is certified.
Permit prose allows up to two years while the earlier fee table describes a one-year CP term; duration is withheld pending issuer reconciliation.
Class C transaction prices and term lengths are dated fee policy and withheld pending current confirmation.
State identification, disability identification, veteran, honorary and National Guard benefits are outside the declared regular driving-credential path.
The foreign-transfer heading includes territories, but its text treats credentials outside the states and District of Columbia as new issuance; territory-specific reciprocity remains unverified.
No complete current list of countries with testing exemptions was supplied on the selected page; no country exemption is authored.
